analysis:
Vertiv fell 13.7%, 9.2 points more than the market and 6.6 points below its AI infrastructure peers (which posted a median decline of 7.1%). The headlines collectively describe a broad selloff in AI-related and data center stocks, with multiple pieces framing this as a second day of declines following election results -- one headline specifically refers to data center stocks being hit by a "Blue Wave," and another mentions "forced control on CapEx." The stock's drop appears more severe than peers in the same theme, though the whole group sold off sharply alongside broader industrial weakness.

The company reported earnings eight days ago on October 28, beating estimates by 21% with an abnormal move beyond the market of 15.5% higher that session. However, the earnings setup shows volatility: across eight reports, all beat estimates, yet four still saw the stock fall the next day, with a typical abnormal move around 5.3%. The stock tends to make significant moves around earnings (median absolute move of 9.2%), and beating hasn't reliably meant gains.
